title: security: RBAC v2 - enforce KMS region residency + audit logging hardening
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated industries require deterministic KMS region residency (KMS keys and crypto operations must be pinned to allowed regions) plus stronger audit trails for KMS-related operations. This change tightens RBAC v2 policy evaluation to enforce residency constraints, adds explicit audit events for KMS operations, and provides a migration path for existing policies.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a KMS residency enforcement layer to the RBAC v2 evaluator (policy predicates + validator), emits structured audit events for KMS API usage (encrypt/decrypt/sign/verify/ key access), introduces a policy migration script to annotate existing policies with residency metadata, updates operator docs, and adds integration tests and end-to-end smoke tests for Dedicated/Private flows. Includes minor API version bump for policy validation responses so clients can surface residency violations.

Checklist: - [x] RBAC evaluator residency predicate implemented - [x] Audit event schema defined and implemented - [x] Integration tests (unit + e2e) added - [x] Migration script for existing policies - [x] Docs and release notes updated - [x] Security review and threat model update completed

Related linear/jira: Linear: ENG-11234, SEC-211. Support escalation: SUP-4032.

Notes for reviewers: The residency check is intentionally strict by default; existing policies without residency metadata are treated as "unspecified" and will be flagged in audit logs and the migration report but not immediately blocked. The operator can enable enforcement via a cluster config flag (rbac.enforce_kms_residency=true). This PR includes a migration helper CLI that will annotate policy YAMLs with a best-effort region mapping (based on project metadata) and produce a dry-run report.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy change under feature flag (enforcement off) for 1 week in staging; 2) Run migration CLI across Dedicated clusters and review the dry-run report; 3) Flip enforcement on for non-production tenants first; 4) Monitor audit logs/alerts and rollback if anomalous spikes; 5) Gradual rollout to production.

Backwards compatibility: Policy evaluation returns a new field in validation responses (residency_status) and a non-breaking default (enforcement disabled). Clients that parse validation responses should tolerate unknown fields.
